explanations.2008-001: The U.S. Constitution is the supreme law of the land; any state or federal law that conflicts with it is not valid.
explanations.2008-002: The U.S. Constitution sets up the government, divides its powers among three branches, and protects the basic rights of the people.
explanations.2008-003: The first three words of the Constitution are 'We the People,' expressing that the power of the government comes from the people.
explanations.2008-004: An amendment is a change to (or an addition of) the Constitution.
explanations.2008-005: The first ten amendments to the Constitution are called the Bill of Rights, which protect basic freedoms and rights.
explanations.2008-006: The First Amendment protects several rights and freedoms — for example, freedom of speech, freedom of religion, freedom of the press, freedom to assemble, and freedom to petition the government.
explanations.2008-008: The Declaration of Independence announced that the colonies were free and independent from Great Britain.
explanations.2008-009: The Declaration of Independence states that all people have the rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.
explanations.2008-010: Freedom of religion means you can practice any religion, or none at all, without government interference.
explanations.2008-011: The U.S. has a capitalist (free market) economy, where businesses and individuals — not the government — make most economic decisions.
explanations.2008-012: The rule of law means everyone — ordinary citizens and government leaders alike — must follow the law; no one is above it.
explanations.2008-013: The U.S. government has three branches — the legislative (Congress), the executive (the President), and the judicial (the courts).
explanations.2008-014: Power is divided among three branches, and each can check the others (checks and balances) so no single branch becomes too powerful.
explanations.2008-015: The President is in charge of the executive branch, which carries out and enforces the laws.
explanations.2008-016: Congress — the legislative branch — makes federal laws.
explanations.2008-017: The U.S. Congress has two parts: the Senate and the House of Representatives.
explanations.2008-018: There are 100 U.S. senators — two for each of the 50 states.
explanations.2008-019: We elect a U.S. senator to serve a term of six years.
explanations.2008-020: This asks for the name of one of your state's current U.S. senators; it changes with elections and differs by where you live. Residents of D.C. and U.S. territories answer that they have no U.S. senators.
explanations.2008-021: The House of Representatives has 435 voting members, with each state's number based on its population.
explanations.2008-022: We elect a U.S. representative to serve a term of two years.
explanations.2008-023: This asks for the name of the person who currently represents your congressional district in the House; it changes with elections and differs by where you live. Residents of some territories may name that territory's nonvoting Delegate or Resident Commissioner instead.
explanations.2008-024: Each U.S. senator represents all the people of their entire state, not just one congressional district.
explanations.2008-025: Some states have more representatives than others because the number is based on population — states with more people get more seats in the House.
